open_obligations: Compare effect sizes: the cited passages give no effect size for Arnesen et al.'s training result, while Khan et al. report judge accuracy against aggregate rating
Confirm both studies measure debater skill by Elo-style win rates on QuALITY-HARD questions with hidden passages

out.other_title: Self-play debate: judge accuracy rises with debater aggregate rating
out.rationale: The authors explicitly say their training result matches the trend Khan et al. found with inference-time optimization. How debater skill is raised and which judge is used both differ, so this corroborates the direction of the trend, not its size.
out.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: Whether stronger debaters yield more accurate judges in debate; holds for training-based optimization, including after mitigating sycophancy bias with a trained judge

text: The authors state that the positive judge-accuracy trend observed for inference-time optimization of debaters (Khan et al., 2024) persists when debaters are trained, and that it persists even after mitigating judge sycophancy with a trained judge.
title: Arnesen et al. find Khan et al.'s debater-skill/judge-accuracy trend persists with debate training
